data.title: Plankton bloom turns Thai island waters a bright, smelly green
data.description: CHON BURI — The sea ‌off Thailand's popular tourist island of Ko Lan turned a bright, pungent green this week as heavy rains and floods helped spark a plankton bloom that kept some swimmers on shore.

data.title: PM ignores  calls to fire  Chadchart
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul rejected calls to remove Bangkok governor Chadchart Sittipunt from his post as the government urged agencies to focus on draining floodwaters and restoring affected areas rather than political criticism.

data.title: Experts urge extra support for elderly
data.description: Thailand needs to strengthen income, healthcare, care and age-friendly systems as the proportion of elderly people is projected to reach nearly one-third of the population by 2042, experts said.

data.title: BMA weighs up car-free days
data.description: The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) may introduce one or two car-free days a week to encourage residents to rely less on private vehicles, as traffic congestion costs the capital an estimated 60 million baht a day.

data.title: Thai Airways to resume normal flight schedules from Saturday
data.description: Thai Airways International (Thai) will return to its normal flight operation mode on Saturday after severe floods in greater Bangkok have maimed the airline as it cancelled some services that stranded passengers and baggage.

data.title: Government launches insurance scheme for 30 million homes
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has launched a nationwide disaster insurance scheme covering some 30 million households.

data.title: Cops widen cross-border scam fight
data.description: The Anti-Cyber Scam Centre (ACSC) is stepping up cooperation with Australia, the United States and neighbouring countries as it shifts its focus from warning victims after they have been defrauded to detecting and disrupting scam networks before losses occur.

data.title: Govt launches insurance scheme for 30m homes
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has launched a nationwide disaster insurance scheme covering some 30 million households.

data.title: Sex workers' group seeks arrests probe
data.description: The Service Workers in Group (Swing) Foundation has called for an investigation into the treatment of 25 sex workers arrested in Pattaya and urged the decriminalisation of consensual sex work to protect their rights.

data.title: Koh Kut tourism outlook brightens amid uncertainty
data.description: Trat: Operators and local officials on Koh Kut expect tourism to recover towards the end of this year and into next year, but remain wary of traveller confidence, the border situation and the island's limited infrastructure.

data.title: City stands  firm on  flood plan
data.description: Bangkok governor Chadchart Sittipunt has defended the city's flood-management strategy, rejecting claims that Bangkok had abandoned its royal "monkey-cheek" water-retention projects.

data.title: Man trapped underground after Sukhumvit landslide
data.description: An emergency rescue was prompted after a man became trapped about three metres underground by a landslide in Soi Pridi Banomyong 14 off Sukhumvit 71 in Bangkok on Thursday evening.

data.title: Chinese and Korean fugitives wanted for fraud arrested in Thailand
data.description: Thai immigration police have arrested a Chinese man accused of a property fraud that caused losses of more than 200 million baht and a South Korean former football coach who had evaded arrest for more than 20 years.

data.title: Hail falls as heavy rain hits parts of Bangkok
data.description: Heavy rain struck several areas of Bangkok on Thursday afternoon, with hail reported along Ratchadaphisek, Lat Phrao and Chok Chai 4 roads, as authorities said a large band of rain was expected over the heart of the capital until 9 pm.

data.title: Three hurt as driver crashes into Guanyin Shrine in Yaowarat
data.description: A driver reportedly lost consciousness and crashed his vehicle into the Guanyin Shrine in Bangkok’s Chinatown on Thursday, injuring three people at the site.

data.title: PM revokes Thai citizenship of Israeli businessman
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has signed an order revoking the Thai citizenship of an Israeli-born man for failing to disclose and renounce other nationalities upon naturalisation.

data.title: Northern water runoff the next challenge
data.description: There will be no heavy rain in the Central Plains, including Bangkok and surrounding provinces, over the next 10 days, but communities in the Chao Phraya basin should prepare for a water runoff influx from northern Thailand, says natural disaster specialist Seree Supratid.

data.title: Phu Kradueng reopens after seasonal closure
data.description: Phu Kradueng National Park has reopened after four-month seasonal closure and is ready to serve up to 3,500 visitors per day, with enhanced security measures.

data.title: Large crocodile killed for safety in flooded Chachoengsao
data.description: CHACHOENGSAO - A large crocodile spotted near a residential area during flooding in Sanam Chai Khet district has been put down by authorities after it was deemed a threat to local residents.

data.title: Another Lao activist disappears in Thailand
data.description: A Lao content creator and activist based in Thailand has not been seen in nearly two weeks and concerns are growing that he may have been abducted or taken back to Laos, a Thailand-based human rights organisation says.

data.title: New accommodation law proposed to replace Hotel Act
data.description: The government has proposed replacing the Hotel Act with a new law designed to bring more accommodation businesses into the regulatory system.

data.title: Bangkok road flooding update
data.description: The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration reported flooding remained on several roads with levels ranging from 5 to 40 centimetres in some northern and eastern areas on Thursday morning.

data.title: Korat farmers struggling with drought
data.description: Nakhon Ratchasima is facing a sharp contrast between flooding and drought, with farmers in Bua Yai struggling to keep rice fields alive while floodwaters recede elsewhere.

data.title: Hua Hin-Cha Am to get Mice status
data.description: Hua Hin–Cha Am has been recognised as a Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions (Mice) City for 2026, bringing together Prachuap Khiri Khan and Phetchaburi as a single business-events destination.

data.title: Group of armed men raid warehouse in Pattani
data.description: A group of armed men raided a warehouse in Pattani early Wednesday, detonating a 10kg homemade bomb, setting fire to a lorry and damaging CCTV cameras. No one was injured.

data.title: PM urges push up value chain
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul presided over the National Economic and Social Development Board's (NESDB) annual meeting to discuss the draft 2028–2032 NESDB plan.

data.title: Govt seeks aid against proxy firms
data.description: The Department of Business Development (DBD) has sent information on more than 100,000 companies with foreign directors or shareholders to 43 embassies, seeking cooperation in tackling nominee businesses.

data.title: Govt eyes new accommodation law
data.description: The government has proposed replacing the Hotel Act with a new law designed to bring more accommodation businesses into the regulatory system.

data.title: Disaster insurance cover rolls out nationwide today
data.description: The government is set to launch a nationwide disaster insurance programme covering about 30 million households from 12am today (Thursday), providing protection against floods, windstorms and earthquakes.

data.title: BMA says it's on top of Chao Phraya water levels
data.description: The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) has assured residents that Chao Phraya water levels remain manageable, as they are already falling in Klong Chan and other flooded areas.

data.title: PM sets up war room for flooding
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has ordered the Disaster Prevention and Mitigation Department to establish a daily flood war room to coordinate nationwide data and speed up emergency responses.

data.title: Court route urged over Senate poll
data.description: A legal forum on the controversial 2024 Senate selection has urged candidates who believe they were adversely affected by alleged systematic collusion to petition the Constitutional Court through the Ombudsman, arguing this could provide a route to challenge the legitimacy of the entire Senate selection process.

data.title: Blame game for floods steps up
data.description: The government failed to manage the flood crisis, issuing warnings too late and responding ineffectively, says People's Party (PP) leader Natthaphong Ruengpanyawut.
